task_commit_basis: merge commit of the reference change (code after the optimization landed), from https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/commit/534d8fcd9e008091ac357446d48df9e505eca87d

reference_change.title: perf: Huge speedup creating wide `Struct` data

workload.command: python -c "import polars as pl; records = [{'s': {f'f{j}': i * 128 + j for j in range(128)}} for i in range(10000)]; pl.DataFrame(records, infer_schema_length=100)"
workload.source: adapted from the timing table in the description of https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/29813 (pl.DataFrame(records, infer_schema_length=100) on records holding a 128-field struct, 10,000 rows)

oracle.source: py-polars's struct tests (py-polars/tests/unit/datatypes/test_struct.py, which https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/29813 extends); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 86×; 02×; 18×; 06×; 07×

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. The Python package is built from source with maturin, as the repository's Makefile does, but with its fast-release profile (release without LTO) to keep the build time down; the Rust toolchain is the tree's pinned nightly-2026-09-01 through rustup. Python and Python dependencies are pinned to the change's era (see eval/README.md, Built and run here)
